name: Saint Raymond Nonnatus
history: A Catalan friar of the Order of Our Lady of Mercy, founded to ransom Christians held captive in North Africa. Tradition holds that he gave himself as a hostage to free others. His name, meaning not born, recalls that he was delivered after his mother died in childbirth, and he is patron of mothers, midwives and the newborn.
life: Raymond was born in Catalonia, and tradition says that he was taken alive from his mother’s womb after she had died, hence the name Nonnatus. As a young man he joined the Mercedarians, founded by Saint Peter Nolasco in 1218, whose members vowed to give themselves as hostages, if need be, to free captives. Sent to North Africa with money for ransoms, he is said to have stayed behind as a hostage when the funds ran out, and to have preached to his fellow prisoners. Tradition holds that his captors pierced his lips and padlocked his mouth to stop him preaching. After his release he returned to Spain. The story goes that he was named a cardinal by Gregory IX and set out for Rome, but fell ill and died near Barcelona in 1240. Much of his life is known only through later tradition. His name was entered in the Roman Martyrology in 1657.
prayerTo: Saint Raymond, you were given life through your mother’s death and gave your own freedom for captives. Pray for expectant mothers and for all who help bring children into the world, for those held captive, and for me, that I may be willing to give something of myself so that others may be free. Amen.
penance: Pray today for expectant mothers and for anyone you know who is awaiting a birth, and give to a charity that supports mothers in need or people held captive.
meditation: The Mercedarians promised to take the place of captives if there was no other way. Who around you is held captive by debt, addiction or fear, and what could you do for them?
prayer: O God, Who made blessed Raymund, Your Confessor, famous for delivering Your faithful from the captivity of the infidels, grant us by his intercession that, having been released from the bonds of our sins, we may with free minds do what is pleasing to You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
